Regulation: B.C. Reg. 103/2026
Made under: Utilities Commission Act
Published in: No. 12 – B.C. Regs. 99 to 109, June 30, 2026
Deposit date: June 24, 2026

B.C. Reg. 103/2026, deposited June 24, 2026, under theUTILITIES COMMISSION ACT[section 22]. Ministerial Order M244/2026, dated June 23, 2026. I, Adrian Dix, Minister of Energy and Climate Solutions, order that the attached FortisBC Inc. Exemption Regulation is made. — A. DIX,Minister of Energy and Climate Solutions. FORTISBC INC.EXEMPTION REGULATION 1In this regulation,"Act"means theUtilities Commission Act. 2(1)	FortisBC Inc. is exempt from section 45 (5) of the Act in respect of the following extensions of its system: (a)	upgrades at the DG Bell substation; (b)	a new substation in the North End neighbourhood of the City of Kelowna. (2)	Subsection (1) does not apply in relation to an extension that, on the date FortisBC Inc. decides to construct the extension, cannot reasonably be expected to come into service by June 30, 2036. minutes_briefs.title: FortisBC exempt from utility approval for Kelowna substation upgrades
minutes_briefs.summary: The B.C. government has issued a regulation that exempts FortisBC Inc. from a specific approval requirement under the Utilities Commission Act for two electrical system upgrades: upgrades at the DG Bell substation and a new substation in Kelowna's North End neighbourhood. Normally, utilities must get approval from the BC Utilities Commission before building or extending their systems. This exemption means FortisBC can proceed with these projects without that approval, as long as they are expected to be in service by June 30, 2036.
minutes_briefs.action_required: No action required for business owners; this is a utility regulatory change.

key_dates.label: FortisBC exemption projects must be in service by June 30, 2036

minutes_briefs.industries: Construction & Development, Landlord & Property Mgmt, Retail
